content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'lucent-prod-vpc' reporting GPU saturation for tenant lucent-corp. 95% queue depth, 400ms tail latency spikes, token errors increasing. Pagerduty incident opened: PD-4521.
oncall-nick: Got the page. I'm on it, joining voice.
sre-ana: I see sustained queue growth on pool lucent-prod-vpc. Metrics: GPU util 98%, queue length ~23, avg dispatch 1.8s. Single tenant (lucent-corp) accounting for ~92% of requests.
sre-ana: Quick mitigation options: 1) enable emergency burst on pool (consumes shared capacity) 2) evict best-effort tenants from nodes backing the pool 3) throttle tenant from routing layer 4) scale-out dedicated pool (provision delay ~6-12m).
sre-ana: Impact: enabling burst will exceed reserved commit and may hit overage billing thresholds; eviction affects other small tenants briefly.
sre-ana: Recommend: enable emergency burst + apply immediate tenant-level rate limit to lucent-corp while infra provisions extra capacity.
oncall-nick: @pm-jess can you approve emergency burst cost for Lucent? They are enterprise customer; acct-ally oncall too.
pm-jess: on phone, approving emergency burst for Lucent for now — escalate billing after stabilised. :thumbsup:
acct-ally: Confirmed Lucent is on enterprise SLA. Approve temporary overage for incident. Notify legal if needed.
sre-ana: Ok executing plan. @eng-runtime-mike please apply routing throttle rule for tenant and enable burst. I'll coordinate scale-out with infra.
eng-runtime-mike: Running commands now. Patching routing rule:
```bash
redwoodctl routes patch --pool lucent-prod-vpc --tenant lucent-corp --throttle "rps:50,burst:100"
```
eng-runtime-mike: Throttle applied. Observability: incoming request rate for lucent-corp dropped ~60% within 20s.
eng-runtime-mike: Enabling emergency burst flag on pool:
```bash
redwoodctl pools update lucent-prod-vpc --emergency-burst true --burst-tenant lucent-corp
```
incident-bot: :information_source: Emergency burst enabled by eng-runtime-mike. Note: CPU/GPU headroom pulled from shared pool.
sre-ana: Requesting infra to provision 4x A100 nodes into lucent-prod-vpc (estimated 8 GPU slots). ETA 8m. @eng-infra (if present) please confirm.
eng-runtime-mike: Triggered infra-provision API: POST /infra/pools/scale?pool=lucent-prod-vpc&count=4 -> request id infra-9981.
eng-runtime-mike: Infra responded provision started, nodes initializing.
support-liz: Heads-up to Lucent AE and support: preparing customer message now. Need short ETA and mitigation summary.
support-liz: Draft to customer: "We're experiencing elevated latency due to your workload exceeding your reserved pool capacity. We've enabled temporary burst and applied rate-limits to stabilize traffic while provisioning additional capacity. ETA 10 minutes. We'll keep you updated." OK to send?
pm-jess: Send it. Keep language simple and own the mitigation.
oncall-nick: Voice update: everyone on call. Monitoring tail latencies. Queue length dropping from 23 -> 9 after throttle/burst.
sre-ana: Good. Observability note: KV cache hit rate unchanged; this is pure request volume. No model OOMs found in logs. Attaching sample logs:
```
[2024-09-21T18:12:03Z] pool=lucent-prod-vpc tenant=lucent-corp dispatch_delay=2.1s gpu_util=99%
[2024-09-21T18:12:21Z] pool=lucent-prod-vpc tenant=lucent-corp dispatch_delay=0.9s gpu_util=94%
```
eng-runtime-mike: Infra nodes coming up, first node joined at +4m. New GPU capacity recognized by runtime; autoscaler reports +2 active nodes so far.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Capacity increased by 4 GPUs; dispatch queue dropped to 2. Latencies returning to baseline.
support-liz: Sent update to Lucent: "We've enabled a temporary throttle and added capacity. Latency should improve within minutes. We'll follow up with a detailed post-incident summary"
acct-ally: Lucent AE acknowledges, appreciates rapid response. No immediate revenue impact reported; they saw some 500s during the peak window.
sre-ana: Quick note: throttling ACL will remain for 30m and then we'll gradually lift as we confirm steady-state. Also scheduling a follow-up rollback plan.
eng-runtime-mike: Rolling back emergency-burst flag after validation:
```bash
redwoodctl pools update lucent-prod-vpc --emergency-burst false
redwoodctl routes patch --pool lucent-prod-vpc --tenant lucent-corp --remove-throttle
```
eng-runtime-mike: Rollback executed. Monitoring shows stable GPU util ~65%, queue 0-1.
oncall-nick: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. I'll keep paging escalation on until EOD local.
pm-jess: Assigning postmortem to @sre-ana and @eng-runtime-mike. Please include: root cause analysis, why autoscaler didn't pre-warm, tenant rate patterns, and recommend protections (burst quotas, predictive scaling, SLA knobs).
sre-ana: Will do. Initial triage notes saved to incident doc: PD-4521.
sre-ana: Suggested short-term product action: consider per-tenant budgeted-burst tokens so one tenant can't completely consume shared pool without explicit overage policy.
acct-ally: Also recommend billing follow-up to discuss burst allowances in contract.
support-liz: Logged customer timeline and message copies in ticket INC-7823.
incident-bot: :page_facing_up: Incident PD-4521 status changed to MITIGATED. Root cause: sudden traffic surge from lucent-corp exceeding reserved pool; autoscaler provisioning lagged behind peak.
oncall-nick: Thanks team. Good coordination. Closing thread after postmortem. :raised_hands:
